description: An agent that operates a graphical interface through screenshots and mouse and keyboard actions, reaching software that has no API.
An agent that acts on web pages, observing them through screenshots, the DOM or the accessibility tree.
A structured list of a page's interactive elements with roles and labels; cheaper and more precise for an agent than pixels.
An agent whose main action is writing and running code, combining several operations per step and keeping intermediate data out of the model's context.
Research showing that executable code as the action space lets agents solve more tasks in fewer steps than JSON tool calls.
An isolated environment for untrusted code: no secrets, limited network egress, resource and time limits, ephemeral per task.
A lightweight virtual machine with its own kernel (Firecracker, for example) that isolates code more strongly than a container.
A rule that lets a sandbox reach only named destinations, so injected instructions cannot send data anywhere else.
